name: Reverse pendulum serve
summary: The pendulum swing reversed: sidespin that kicks the other way.
whenToUse: To mix with your normal pendulum serve so the receiver can't settle on one spin direction.

keyPoints.stance: Side-on or slightly open, in the backhand corner.
keyPoints.bodyAction: Turn with the swing; knees bent to keep the contact low.
keyPoints.strokeLength: The bat swings from left to right across the body (right-hander).
keyPoints.timing: Contact as the ball falls, near table height.
keyPoints.tablePosition: Backhand corner, behind the end line.
keyPoints.freeArm: Legal toss, then out of the way.
keyPoints.batArm: Elbow up, bat face turned out; contact on the left side of the ball (right side if left-handed).
keyPoints.recovery: Step back into ready quickly; the return often goes cross-court.
keyPoints.anticipation: The return tends to go to your forehand side: be ready for it.

cues: Brush the far side of the ball

learningPath.task: Watch the reverse swing from the front.
learningPath.passCheck: You can say the three cues.
3 sets of 10, then yes to all self-checks.
selfChecks: Did the bat swing left to right (right-hander)?

learningPath.task: Serve reverse sidespin; watch the kick.
Short reverse serves to a target.
Alternate normal and reverse pendulum, hiding which is coming.
Serve and attack the third ball.
learningPath.passCheck: 6 of 10 third balls on the table.

gamePatterns.situation: Your normal sidespin serve is being read.
gamePatterns.how: Switch to the reverse: the return comes out the other side, so prepare your third ball there.

fixes: Brush the far side of the ball
Turn the face out before contact
Lift the elbow to shoulder height

penholdNotes: Penholders turn the wrist further; the contact idea is the same.
